mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an accommodative monetary policy stance that reduces discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.0% in a single month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.0%, or Rank IC for the trigger condition is negative over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential investment (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicate a broad-based weakening in private demand, triggering recessionary expectations and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or Rank IC for the joint decline condition is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high industrial production growth (INDPRO > 1.5% month-over-month), supply chain bottlenecks ease and corporate output increases, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO growth exceeds 1.5% m/m, or Rank IC for the regime is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) over the past quarter signals strong labor market conditions that boost consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS rises, or Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) rises above 3.0% year-over-year, it signals accelerating inflation that prompts the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL exceeds 3.0% y/y, or Rank IC for the trigger condition is negative over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) indicate a severe supply-side shock that disrupts economic activity, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both INDPRO and HOUST decline, or Rank IC for the joint decline condition is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 4.0% year-over-year), the Federal Reserve maintains restrictive monetary policy that suppresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL exceeds 4.0% y/y, or Rank IC for the regime is below 0.03 over a 3-year rolling window.
